Get or set global options for argitect()

Source: R/0_global.R
argitect_options.Rd

Get or set global options used by argitect(). This function is backed by GlobalOptions::setGlobalOptions(), so options can be read and written with argitect_options("name"), argitect_options("name" = value), argitect_options(name = value) or argitect_options$name.

Usage

argitect_options(
  ...,
  RESET = FALSE,
  READ.ONLY = NULL,
  LOCAL = FALSE,
  ADD = FALSE
)

argitect.options(
  ...,
  RESET = FALSE,
  READ.ONLY = NULL,
  LOCAL = FALSE,
  ADD = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Named options to set, or a single option name to get.

RESET

Whether to reset all options to their default values.

READ.ONLY

Passed to GlobalOptions::setGlobalOptions().

LOCAL

Passed to GlobalOptions::setGlobalOptions().

ADD

Passed to GlobalOptions::setGlobalOptions().

Value

The current option value (when getting) or, invisibly, the full option list (when setting).

Details

Supported options:

  • config A character vector of parser configuration flags. The following values are recognized:

    • "bundling": allow single-letter flags to be combined, so that -abc is the same as -a -b -c (this is the default behavior).

    • "no_bundling": disable bundling; -abc is then treated as a single (unknown) option named abc.

    • "ignore_case": match long option names case-insensitively, so that --FOO matches --foo (by default matching is case-sensitive).

    • "no_ignore_case": keep case-sensitive matching; if both "ignore_case" and "no_ignore_case" are given, the latter wins.

    For example argitect_options("config" = c("ignore_case", "no_bundling")).

  • template_tag The tag identifying specifications in a template, in the format "left_tag CODE right_tag" (default "<CODE>").

  • help_style The style of the help message: "one-column" or "two-column".

  • help_width The width of the help message, as a vector of one or two numbers (default c(90, 40)). The first number is the total width; the one-column style uses only it. The second number is the width of the first (option) column used by the two-column style. Option names that are too long are wrapped, and continuation lines are aligned with the second option name.

  • value_sep The separator used to split multiple values inside a single name=value pair for a vector sub-argument. The default "auto" automatically detects the separator among ",", ";", ":", "|" and "/" by picking the one that satisfies the type and count constraints.

argitect_options(...) should be put before calling argitect().

Examples

argitect_options("help_width")
#> [1] 90 40
old = argitect_options("help_width")
argitect_options("help_width" = 100)
argitect_options("help_width")
#> [1] 100
argitect_options("help_width" = old)
